descripcion_geo: Tectonic depression that extends from the Galilee Sea to the Gulf of Aqaba, passing through the Dead Sea. Includes the Jordan Valley.
importancia_estrategica: Palestine north-south corridor; caravan route and natural border between the West Bank and Transjordan.

historias.titulo: Israel walks across the Arabah towards the Jordan
historias.descripcion: Israel marches across the Arabah from Sinai to the fields of Moab, where it will wait to cross the Jordan.

historias.titulo: The last northern Israelites flee to the Arabah
historias.descripcion: After the fall of Samaria, groups of northern Israelites flee to the Arabah seeking to escape Assyrian deportation.

historias.titulo: John the Baptist in Jordanian Arabah
historias.descripcion: John baptizes in Bethábara/Betania on the other side of the Jordan, in the Arabá area.

personajes.descripcion: He led Israel through the Arabah; the 'fields of Moab in the Arabah' were his final resting place.
He baptized in the Jordan in the Arabah area.
He crossed the Arabá to begin the conquest of Canaan from the fields of Moab.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: The great geographical corridor of the holy land; scene of the final exodus and the ministry of John the Baptist next to the Jordan.

judaismo.descripcion: The Arabah was the last leg of the pilgrimage: Israel traveled it before crossing the Jordan towards the promised land.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The Arabah was the last leg of the pilgrimage: Israel traveled it before crossing the Jordan towards the promised land.

cristianismo.fuente_primaria: Nuevo Testamento / Padres de la Iglesia
cristianismo.descripcion: John the Baptist baptized in the Jordanian Arabah: the new spiritual exodus of Israel.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: John the Baptist baptized in the Jordanian Arabah: the new spiritual exodus of Israel.
